properties.text: encode_internal_node must accept only valid node types: None, LeafNode, ExtensionNode, or BranchNode. Any other input type must trigger an AssertionError, ensuring no unexpected node types can be injected into the trie structure.

reachability.notes: Attacker can submit transactions that trigger state trie modifications. If a crafted transaction results in an unexpected node type being passed to encode_internal_node, the trie could become corrupted. Reachable via any transaction that modifies account state.

properties.severity_justification: A violation would allow injection of arbitrary data into the state trie, potentially corrupting the state root and causing consensus splits between clients that handle the invalid type differently.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating injection of an invalid node type that causes divergent state roots across execution clients.

properties.text: For encode_internal_node, if the RLP encoding of a node is less than 32 bytes, the unencoded form must be returned; if >= 32 bytes, the keccak256 hash of the encoding must be returned. This threshold behavior must be deterministic across all clients.

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft transactions that produce trie nodes near the 32-byte boundary. If implementations disagree on the threshold comparison (< vs <=), a consensus split occurs.

properties.severity_justification: Any inconsistency in the 32-byte threshold check between execution clients would produce different state roots for the same block, causing a network-wide consensus failure.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating a transaction that produces a trie node at exactly the 32-byte boundary triggering divergent behavior across clients.

properties.text: encode_node must require a non-None storage_root when encoding an Account node. Attempting to encode an Account with storage_root == None must trigger an assertion failure.

reachability.notes: This is an internal invariant within the state trie encoding pipeline. An external attacker cannot directly control whether storage_root is None; this depends on the execution client's internal account management logic.

properties.severity_justification: If an Account is encoded without a valid storage_root, the resulting state trie root would be incorrect, potentially causing silent data corruption or consensus failures.

properties.text: encode_node must correctly fall back to previous_trie.encode_node for unrecognized node types, ensuring backward compatibility across fork transitions (e.g., Osaka inheriting encoding rules from prior forks).

reachability.notes: During fork transitions, historical state data may contain node types defined in earlier forks. An attacker could interact with contracts that have state from pre-Osaka forks to trigger the fallback path.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect fallback behavior during fork transitions could cause silent state root divergence between clients that handle the fallback differently.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating state encoded incorrectly during or after fork transition due to fallback path error.

properties.text: copy_trie must perform a shallow copy of trie._data such that the original and copied tries share frozen object references but mutations to one do not affect the other.

reachability.notes: copy_trie is invoked during begin_transaction for snapshot creation. An attacker crafting transactions with nested CALL operations triggers snapshot creation. If copies are not isolated, rollback_transaction restores corrupted state.

properties.severity_justification: If copy_trie produces a non-isolated copy, nested call reverts (REVERT opcode) would fail to properly restore state, allowing an attacker to persist unauthorized state changes across reverted sub-calls. This directly enables fund theft via state manipulation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating state mutation persistence across a reverted nested call due to shallow copy aliasing.

properties.text: trie_set must represent default values by absence from trie._data: setting a key to the trie's default value must delete the key from _data, and setting a non-default value must insert or update the key.

reachability.notes: Every SSTORE operation in the EVM triggers trie_set. An attacker can set storage slots to zero (the default value for storage tries) via smart contract interactions, which should trigger key deletion.

properties.severity_justification: If default-value keys are not properly deleted, the state trie will contain spurious entries, inflating state size and potentially causing gas refund miscalculations (EIP-2200/3529 gas refund rules depend on whether a slot transitions to/from zero).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing incorrect gas refund behavior or state bloat due to non-deletion of default-value keys.

properties.text: trie_set invariant: setting a key to the default value when the key already exists in _data must delete that key; setting a key to the default value when the key does not exist must be a no-op.

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft transactions that set storage to zero for both existing and non-existing keys, triggering both branches of this invariant.

properties.severity_justification: Violation would cause non-deterministic trie mutations: deleting a non-existent key could panic or corrupt internal data structures, while failing to delete an existing default-value key leads to state root divergence.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing state root divergence from incorrect default-value handling in trie_set.

properties.text: trie_get must return trie.default for any key not present in trie._data, and the stored value for any key that is present.

reachability.notes: Every SLOAD operation reads from the trie via trie_get. An attacker can read arbitrary storage slots via smart contract interactions.

properties.severity_justification: If trie_get returns incorrect values (non-default for missing keys or wrong values for existing keys), all smart contract execution that reads state would produce incorrect results, potentially enabling unauthorized fund transfers.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating incorrect SLOAD return value caused by trie_get bug.

properties.text: common_prefix_length must return a value in the range [0, min(len(a), len(b))] for all inputs. The return value must never exceed the length of either input sequence.

reachability.notes: common_prefix_length is used during patricialize to determine trie structure. Attacker-controlled storage keys (via SSTORE) determine the nibble sequences passed to this function.

properties.severity_justification: An out-of-bounds return value would cause incorrect trie structuring during patricialize, leading to corrupted state roots and consensus failures.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing specially crafted storage key patterns that trigger an off-by-one or bounds violation in common_prefix_length.

properties.text: common_prefix_length must satisfy: for all j < return_value, a[j] == b[j]. The returned prefix length must represent a genuine common prefix with no mismatched elements.

reachability.notes: Storage key selection by attackers controls the nibble sequences being compared. Incorrect prefix length determination leads to wrong trie node types (Extension vs Branch).

properties.severity_justification: An incorrect common prefix length would cause patricialize to create wrong node types (ExtensionNode where BranchNode is needed or vice versa), corrupting the trie structure and producing incorrect state roots.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating incorrect trie structure generation from a prefix length miscalculation.

properties.text: All nibble values in the input to nibble_list_to_compact must be in the range [0, 15]. Values outside this range must not be accepted as valid nibbles.

reachability.notes: Nibble values are derived from byte decomposition in bytes_to_nibble_list which always produces values in [0,15] by construction (high nibble masking and shifting). External attackers cannot inject invalid nibbles.

properties.severity_justification: An internal bug producing out-of-range nibbles would corrupt compact encoding, leading to non-decodable trie nodes. Impact is limited to state corruption detectable at the next state root verification.

properties.text: The high nibble of the first byte in nibble_list_to_compact output must correctly encode the is_leaf flag and parity: even length with is_leaf=true yields 0x20, even length with is_leaf=false yields 0x00, odd length with is_leaf=true yields 0x3X, odd length with is_leaf=false yields 0x1X.

reachability.notes: The compact encoding determines how trie nodes are serialized and deserialized. Incorrect flag encoding would cause trie traversal to misidentify leaf vs extension nodes, corrupting lookups.

properties.severity_justification: Misencoding the is_leaf flag causes trie deserialization to treat extension nodes as leaf nodes and vice versa. This corrupts all subsequent trie lookups and produces incorrect state roots, causing consensus failure across all transactions.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating state trie corruption from is_leaf flag misencoding during compact encoding.

properties.text: The output length of nibble_list_to_compact must be exactly ceil((len(x) + 1) / 2) for all valid inputs.

reachability.notes: Incorrect output length would cause RLP encoding to produce wrong byte counts, affecting the 32-byte threshold in encode_internal_node and ultimately state root computation.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect compact encoding length affects RLP serialization, which in turn affects the hash-vs-inline decision in encode_internal_node. This could cause state root divergence between clients.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing state root divergence from incorrect compact encoding length.

properties.text: bytes_to_nibble_list output length must be exactly 2 * len(input) for all inputs. Each input byte must produce exactly two nibbles.

reachability.notes: Trie keys (account addresses, storage keys) are converted to nibble lists via this function. Incorrect length would misalign all trie lookups and insertions.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect nibble list length would cause all trie path computations to be wrong, completely corrupting the state trie structure and producing incorrect state roots for every block.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating trie corruption from incorrect nibble list length.

properties.text: Each output nibble from bytes_to_nibble_list must be in the range [0, 15]. The high nibble extraction (byte & 0xF0) >> 4 and low nibble extraction (byte & 0x0F) must produce valid nibble values for all byte values.

reachability.notes: All 256 possible byte values can appear in trie keys. The bitwise operations must correctly decompose every byte into two valid nibbles.

properties.severity_justification: The bitwise operations are mathematically guaranteed to produce values in [0,15] for any byte input. A violation would require a fundamental arithmetic bug in the implementation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing out-of-range nibble production for a specific byte value.

properties.text: bytes_to_nibble_list and nibble_list_to_compact must be inverse operations (modulo the compact header byte). Converting bytes to nibbles and then back via compact encoding with appropriate is_leaf flag must yield data recoverable to the original bytes.

reachability.notes: Round-trip correctness is essential for trie serialization and deserialization. An attacker can trigger arbitrary key paths through state modifications.

properties.severity_justification: If the nibble/compact encoding round-trip is not lossless, trie deserialization produces different keys than were stored, causing phantom state entries, missing state, or corrupted lookups. This would cause consensus failures.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating data corruption from round-trip encoding/decoding failure.

properties.text: In _prepare_trie, all encoded values in the output mapping must be non-empty. An empty encoded value (b"") must trigger an AssertionError, preventing empty values from entering the patricialize pipeline.

reachability.notes: An attacker could craft transactions that result in accounts or storage values that encode to empty bytes, which should be caught by this assertion.

properties.severity_justification: Empty values in the trie would produce malformed trie nodes during patricialize, leading to unpredictable behavior in encode_internal_node and potential state root divergence.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing empty encoded value bypassing the assertion check.

properties.text: In _prepare_trie, when trie.secured is True, all keys must be hashed with keccak256 before conversion to nibble lists. When trie.secured is False, keys must be used as-is.

reachability.notes: The state trie (accounts) uses secured mode (keccak256 hashed keys) while the storage trie uses unsecured mode. Incorrect mode handling would produce wrong key paths.

properties.severity_justification: If the secured flag is not correctly applied, the trie would use unhashed keys for the state trie (or hashed keys for storage), producing completely different trie structures and state roots, causing immediate consensus failure.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating state root divergence from incorrect secured/unsecured key handling.

properties.text: In _prepare_trie, Account values must have a get_storage_root callback available. Attempting to encode an Account without the callback must be prevented.

reachability.notes: The get_storage_root callback is provided by the execution client's state management layer. An external attacker cannot control whether this callback is present.

properties.severity_justification: A missing storage root callback would cause an account to be encoded without its storage root, resulting in incorrect state trie entries and potential fund loss if account balances are misrepresented.

properties.text: The root function must return EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT (keccak256(RLP(b''))) when the trie is empty (no entries in _data).

reachability.notes: An attacker can create contracts that SELFDESTRUCT (or have all storage cleared), resulting in empty storage tries. The root of an empty storage trie must match the canonical EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT.

properties.severity_justification: An incorrect empty trie root would cause every account with no storage to have a wrong storage_root in its RLP encoding, causing state root divergence for every block that processes such accounts.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing incorrect empty trie root computation.

properties.text: The root function must always return a 32-byte value, regardless of trie contents. For tries where the RLP-encoded root node is < 32 bytes, keccak256 must be applied; for >= 32 bytes, the root node is already a hash.

reachability.notes: Small tries (few entries) can produce root nodes with RLP encoding < 32 bytes. An attacker can create such tries via minimal storage usage in contracts.

properties.severity_justification: If the root is not always 32 bytes, the account RLP encoding will have incorrect storage_root length, corrupting the state trie and causing consensus failures across all clients.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating non-32-byte root value returned from the root function.

properties.text: In the root function, when the RLP encoding of root_node is >= 32 bytes, root_node must be of type Bytes (not a complex tuple/list type).

reachability.notes: This invariant ensures encode_internal_node has already hashed large nodes into Bytes. Violation would mean the root function returns a non-hash value that is >= 32 bytes RLP-encoded.

properties.severity_justification: Returning a non-Bytes root_node when >= 32 bytes would produce an inconsistent state root representation, potentially causing type errors or incorrect hash computation in downstream consumers.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating a trie state that produces a non-Bytes root_node with >= 32 byte RLP encoding.

properties.text: patricialize must return None when the input object is empty (len(obj) == 0). This is the base case for trie construction from an empty dataset.

reachability.notes: Empty subtries are common in the patricialize recursion. An attacker can trigger this by creating accounts/contracts with minimal state.

properties.severity_justification: If patricialize does not return None for empty input, the trie would contain spurious nodes for empty branches, producing incorrect state roots.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing non-None return for empty patricialize input.

properties.text: patricialize must return a LeafNode when the input object contains exactly one element (len(obj) == 1). The leaf must contain the key suffix from the current level and the associated value.

reachability.notes: Single-element subtries arise when trie paths diverge to unique keys. Common in storage tries with few entries.

properties.severity_justification: Returning a wrong node type for single-element objects would corrupt the trie structure. The key suffix must correctly represent the remaining path from the current level.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing incorrect LeafNode construction for single-element patricialize input.

properties.text: patricialize must produce an ExtensionNode when all keys in the object share a common prefix of length > 0 at the current level. The extension must recurse with level increased by the prefix length.

reachability.notes: An attacker can choose storage keys with shared prefixes (e.g., keys starting with 0x00000...) to force ExtensionNode creation.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect ExtensionNode construction would produce the wrong trie structure for key sets with shared prefixes, leading to state root divergence.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating incorrect extension node generation for keys with shared prefixes.

properties.text: patricialize must produce a BranchNode with exactly 16 subnodes when the keys in the object share no common prefix (prefix_length == 0) at the current level.

reachability.notes: An attacker can select storage keys with diverse first nibbles to force BranchNode creation at the root level.

properties.severity_justification: BranchNode must have exactly 16 subnodes (one per nibble value 0-15). Any deviation would produce a structurally invalid trie that cannot be correctly traversed.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing BranchNode with wrong number of subnodes.

properties.text: In patricialize, Account, Receipt, and Uint typed values must not appear at internal branch value positions (len(key) == level). These types are only valid as leaf values. Violation must trigger an AssertionError.

reachability.notes: Branch value positions only occur when a key is a prefix of another key in the trie. For secured tries (keccak256 hashed keys), this is cryptographically infeasible. For unsecured storage tries, storage keys are always 32 bytes and cannot be prefixes of each other.

properties.severity_justification: This assertion guards against structurally invalid trie construction. In practice, this condition cannot be triggered by external input due to key length constraints.

properties.text: patricialize recursive calls must strictly increase the level parameter, ensuring termination. Each recursive call must have level > level_of_caller.

reachability.notes: An attacker choosing specific key patterns could potentially create conditions where the prefix_length is 0 and level does not advance, causing infinite recursion and node crash.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to strictly increase level would cause infinite recursion, crashing the execution client during state root computation. This is a denial-of-service vector for individual nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing key patterns that cause non-terminating patricialize recursion.

properties.text: The RLP encoding of account data in encode_account must use the canonical tuple ordering (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash). Any deviation in field ordering must cause consensus failure.

reachability.notes: Every transaction that modifies account state (balance transfers, contract creation, storage modifications) triggers account encoding. Incorrect field ordering produces different RLP bytes and thus different state roots.

properties.severity_justification: Non-canonical RLP field ordering would produce different account hashes across clients, causing an immediate and total consensus failure for every block.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating wrong field ordering in RLP account encoding.

properties.text: The storage_root parameter passed to encode_account must be a valid 32-byte Merkle root. The function must not validate this value internally, placing the burden on the caller to provide correctness.

reachability.notes: The storage_root is computed by the execution client's state management layer from the account's storage trie. An external attacker cannot directly supply an arbitrary storage_root.

properties.severity_justification: An incorrect storage_root in the account encoding would mean the state trie references a wrong storage trie, potentially making account storage inaccessible or returning wrong values.

properties.text: The deposit event data extracted by extract_deposit_data must have exactly 576 bytes with rigidly defined offsets (PUBKEY_OFFSET=160, WC_OFFSET=256, AMOUNT_OFFSET=320, SIGNATURE_OFFSET=384, INDEX_OFFSET=512). Any deviation must result in InvalidBlock.

reachability.notes: An attacker can interact with the deposit contract to generate deposit events. If extract_deposit_data does not rigorously validate the event data format, malformed deposits could corrupt the beacon chain's validator set.

properties.severity_justification: Parsing deposit data with incorrect offsets could result in wrong BLS public keys, withdrawal credentials, or amounts being passed to the consensus layer, potentially enabling unauthorized validator registrations or fund misappropriation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating malformed deposit event that bypasses offset validation and corrupts deposit data.

properties.text: The deposit event must only be recognized from logs emitted by the canonical DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS (0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa) matching DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH. Logs from any other address or with different event signatures must be ignored.

reachability.notes: An attacker could deploy a contract that emits events with the same signature hash from a different address, attempting to inject fake deposits.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting deposits from a non-canonical contract address would allow an attacker to inject arbitrary validator registrations into the beacon chain, potentially gaining consensus power without actual stake.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating deposit injection from a non-canonical contract address.

properties.text: Receipt processing order (block_output.receipt_keys) must be deterministic across all execution clients. All compliant clients must iterate receipt keys in the same order to produce identical deposit_requests bytes.

reachability.notes: An attacker can submit multiple deposit transactions in a single block, and the ordering of receipt processing determines the deposit request ordering passed to the consensus layer.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic receipt processing order would cause different execution clients to produce different deposit_requests bytes, resulting in different requests_hash values and consensus failure at the EL-CL boundary.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating receipt key ordering divergence between execution clients.

properties.text: trie_get must return a valid (non-None) receipt for every key in block_output.receipt_keys. A None return must trigger an assertion failure rather than silently skipping the receipt.

reachability.notes: Receipt keys are generated by the block builder during block construction and correspond to transactions in the block. An external attacker cannot directly control which keys are queried from the receipts trie.

properties.severity_justification: Silently skipping a receipt with deposit events would cause deposits to be lost, preventing validators from being registered. The assertion failure is the correct behavior to halt and alert rather than proceed with incomplete data.

properties.text: compute_requests_hash must produce identical SHA-256 hashes for identical request inputs across all execution client implementations. The two-level hashing construction (hash each request individually, then combine) must be deterministic.

reachability.notes: The requests_hash is computed from transaction receipts which are attacker-influenced. If different clients compute different hashes for the same receipts, the EL-CL interface breaks.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic requests_hash computation at the EL-CL boundary would cause the consensus layer to reject valid execution payloads (or accept invalid ones), causing network-wide consensus failure.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating requests_hash divergence between execution clients for identical block inputs.

properties.text: The keccak256 hash function used for trie key hashing (secured tries), code_hash computation, and internal node hashing must be collision-resistant and preimage-resistant across all execution client implementations.

reachability.notes: All state trie operations depend on keccak256 for key hashing and node inlining decisions. A collision would allow two different accounts to map to the same trie path.

properties.severity_justification: A keccak256 collision in trie key hashing would allow an attacker to overwrite another account's state, enabling fund theft. A preimage attack could allow forging state proofs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating a keccak256 collision or implementation inconsistency affecting trie key derivation.

properties.text: EIP-7702 Authorization signature verification must validate chain_id for replay protection and nonce for freshness. A signed authorization for one chain must not be replayable on another chain.

reachability.notes: An attacker can capture a valid EIP-7702 authorization signed for one chain and attempt to replay it on another chain. The chain_id and nonce fields must prevent this.

properties.severity_justification: If cross-chain replay protection is missing, an attacker could replay an authorization on a different chain, gaining unauthorized control over the victim's account on that chain.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating cross-chain replay of EIP-7702 authorization.

properties.text: Under EIP-7702, a delegated contract must not be able to modify the delegating EOA's state (balance, nonce, storage) in ways not explicitly authorized by the delegation. The authorization scope must be clearly bounded.

reachability.notes: An attacker could deploy a malicious contract and trick users into delegating code execution to it. The delegation mechanism must have proper scope limits.

properties.severity_justification: If EIP-7702 delegation allows unbounded access to the delegator's account state, a malicious delegation target could drain the account's entire balance.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Note: EIP-7702 by design gives full access to the EOA state. The property verifies that this scope is at least correctly documented and bounded by the authorization mechanism.

properties.text: The snapshot mechanism (begin_transaction/commit_transaction/rollback_transaction) must correctly isolate transient storage (TSTORE/TLOAD) state. Snapshots must include transient storage copies, and rollback must restore transient storage from the snapshot.

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft transactions with nested calls using TSTORE followed by REVERT, testing whether transient storage changes persist across reverts.

properties.severity_justification: If transient storage is not properly snapshotted/restored during nested call reverts, it could leak information between call frames or allow state manipulation across reverted calls.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating transient storage state leaking across a reverted nested call.

properties.text: Pre-EIP-155 transactions (signing_hash_pre155) must not include chain_id in the signed payload. Post-EIP-155 transactions must include chain_id. All post-EIP-155 transaction types (2930, 1559, 4844, 7702) must include chain_id in their signing hashes.

reachability.notes: Pre-EIP-155 transactions are a known attack vector for cross-chain replay. An attacker captures a valid transaction on one chain and replays it on another.

properties.severity_justification: Missing chain_id in signing hashes enables cross-chain replay attacks. While pre-EIP-155 is a known limitation, any new transaction type missing chain_id would be a critical regression.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating cross-chain transaction replay for a post-EIP-155 transaction type.

properties.text: The EMPTY_ACCOUNT constant must be immutable (frozen) at the module level. Any mutation of this sentinel value must be prevented by the @slotted_freezable decorator.

reachability.notes: EMPTY_ACCOUNT is a reference implementation constant. Mutation would require internal code changes, not external input.

properties.severity_justification: This is a reference implementation correctness property. The sentinel value is used for comparisons; mutation would cause incorrect account existence checks but requires internal access.

properties.text: Type aliases (Address=Bytes20, Root=Hash32, VersionedHash=Hash32, Bloom=Bytes256) must enforce byte-length constraints at construction time. Any value with incorrect byte length must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Attacker-controlled transaction data is decoded into typed values. Incorrect length enforcement could allow truncated or oversized addresses/hashes to be accepted.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting wrong-length addresses or hashes could cause fund loss (sending to truncated addresses), state corruption (wrong-length roots), or consensus failures.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating acceptance of wrong-length typed value through the transaction processing pipeline.

properties.text: Transient storage must be completely cleared between transactions. No transient storage state from one transaction may be visible to the next transaction in the same block.

reachability.notes: An attacker can submit two transactions in the same block: one that writes to transient storage and one that reads from the same slot, testing whether state persists across transaction boundaries.

properties.severity_justification: If transient storage leaks between transactions, it violates the fundamental EIP-1153 invariant and could enable information disclosure or cross-transaction state manipulation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating transient storage state persistence across transaction boundaries within the same block.

properties.text: begin_transaction must create deep copies of the main trie, all per-address storage tries, and transient storage via copy_trie. Shallow copies that share mutable internal state are insufficient.

reachability.notes: Every CALL, DELEGATECALL, STATICCALL, and CREATE operation triggers begin_transaction. An attacker can construct complex nested call patterns to test copy isolation.

properties.severity_justification: Shallow snapshot copies would allow state mutations from reverted sub-calls to persist, enabling unauthorized state changes including fund theft via reentrancy-like attacks at the trie level.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating state persistence across rollback_transaction due to shallow copy aliasing in begin_transaction.

properties.text: commit_transaction and rollback_transaction must each pop exactly one snapshot from the snapshot stack. Double-pops, missed pops, or out-of-order pops must not occur.

reachability.notes: Complex nested call patterns with mixed successful and reverted calls stress-test the snapshot stack management.

properties.severity_justification: Snapshot stack corruption would cause state from wrong nesting levels to be restored or committed, enabling unauthorized state changes across call boundaries.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating snapshot stack corruption from nested call patterns.

properties.text: The RLP encoding used throughout the trie (encode_internal_node, encode_node, encode_account) must be deterministic and canonical. Given the same input, all execution clients must produce identical RLP byte sequences.

reachability.notes: Any non-determinism in RLP encoding would directly produce different state roots between clients. Edge cases include empty strings, large integers, and nested structures.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic RLP encoding is the most direct path to consensus failure. Even a single-byte difference in encoding produces a different keccak256 hash and thus a different state root.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating RLP encoding divergence between execution clients for a specific trie node input.

properties.text: The trie must maintain consistency between trie_set and trie_get: for any key k and value v where v != trie.default, immediately after trie_set(trie, k, v), trie_get(trie, k) must return v.

reachability.notes: Every SSTORE followed by SLOAD in the same transaction tests this property. An attacker can craft arbitrary set/get sequences via smart contract code.

properties.severity_justification: If trie_set and trie_get are inconsistent, smart contract state reads would return wrong values, enabling arbitrary contract logic manipulation and potential fund theft.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating SLOAD returning wrong value after SSTORE in the same transaction.

properties.text: The close_state function must properly release all resources (trie snapshots, transient storage, etc.) after transaction processing completes, preventing resource leaks that could exhaust node memory over time.

reachability.notes: An attacker can submit many transactions with deep nesting to create many snapshots, testing whether close_state properly cleans up all allocated resources.

properties.severity_justification: Resource leaks would cause gradual memory exhaustion, eventually crashing the node. This is a DoS vector but requires sustained attack over many blocks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating measurable memory leak from repeated transaction processing.

properties.text: Gas costs for CALL/CREATE operations that trigger nested transactions (and thus trie snapshots) must economically limit nesting depth. The TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT (EIP-7825: 16777216) must bound the total gas available for nested snapshot creation.

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft transactions with maximum nesting depth within the gas limit. Each nesting level creates a trie deep copy, consuming memory proportional to state size.

properties.severity_justification: If the gas cost of nested calls does not adequately reflect the memory cost of trie deep copies, an attacker could exhaust node memory within a single transaction.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating memory exhaustion from deeply nested calls within the gas limit.

properties.text: The validator/block builder ordering of transactions must not affect the determinism of the final state root. Different transaction orderings produce different intermediate states but the trie operations (set/get/copy) must all be deterministic regardless of the ordering.

reachability.notes: Block builders choose transaction ordering. All validators processing the same block with the same transaction order must arrive at the same state root.

properties.severity_justification: If trie operations produce non-deterministic results for a given sequence of operations, validators would compute different state roots for the same block, causing consensus failure.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating non-deterministic state root from identical transaction sequences.
